title: Me caés bien
desc: One verb between a friendship and a declaration
setting: You have been trying to tell Roberto you like him for a full minute and his face has changed.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: ¿Cómo que yo te gusto? Ideay, maje.
steps.en: What do you mean you fancy me? Ideay, maje.

options.es: No, no. Quise decir que me caés bien.
options.en: No, no. I meant that I like you.
options.feedback: Caer bien is liking a person. Gustar with a person is wanting them, and there is no soft version of that mistake.

options.en: That you are a good sort.
options.feedback: True and it changes the subject. The word you actually needed was caer.
You have now said it twice. Whatever happens next, this is the story he tells for the rest of the year.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Ah, que te caigo bien. Eso es otra cosa, maje.
steps.en: Ah, that you like me. That is a different thing entirely, maje.

options.feedback: Take the correction and laugh at it. Nothing fixes a mistake here faster than agreeing it was funny.

options.en: Sorry, I still get it wrong.
options.feedback: Honest. There was nothing to apologise for and he had already forgiven it.

options.en: In English it is the same.
options.feedback: It is not, and explaining your own language is a slow way out of a joke.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: ¿Y quién más te cae bien de aquí?
steps.en: And who else around here do you like?

options.es: Doña Chepa me cae muy bien. Habla con todo el mundo.
options.en: I like doña Chepa a lot. She talks to everybody.
options.feedback: You used it about somebody else straight away. The second time you say a word is when it becomes yours.
Safe. He was hoping for a name and something about them.
Doña Chepa is sixty and this street has a very fast postal service.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.es: Ya pues, vos también me caés bien.
steps.en: Right then, I like you too.

options.es: Qué bueno, porque no me pienso ir.
options.en: Good, because I am not planning on leaving.
options.feedback: He said the thing he does not say often. Answering warmly without making it heavy is exactly the right size.
Fine, and slightly formal for a friend who has just spent ten minutes teasing you.
You did not, and he has just said something he meant. Take it.
